Every 5.5 minutes, whether the vehicle moves or not, and whenever pressure changes significantly. Reads the pressure in steps of 0.1 bar (about 1.5 psi): a tyre between two steps can read one step lower when cold, and the next one up once warm

Every minute while the wheel rotates. While stationary, only when the pressure is below ~22 psi, and in either case, whenever pressure changes significantly. Reads the pressure in steps of about 0.45 psi (3.1 kPa), shown rounded to 0.1 psi: a steady tyre can go back and forth by one step

Experimental. Shows \"Leak?\" under a tyre losing pressure while riding, and notifies about it: its pressure falling from its highest reading of the ride by at least the minimum drop, on two readings in a row, while the tyre isn\'t cooling down.\n\nRiding warms a tyre up, which only raises its pressure, so a fall is air getting out. A leak too slow to show within a ride is left to the low pressure alert, once the tyre is cold. Letting air out shows as a loss too.

If the app does not show the sensor updating as often as you think it should, it could be due to the following reasons:

1. The sensor is not sending any updates at all. You can verify that by briefly taking it off the wheel: it should sense 0 pressure, which should force an update, and the app should show an alert. If it does not, either the sensor itself or its battery may be dead.

2. The sensor is sending updates, but they are not getting to the phone. Changing the phone's position relative to the wheel may help, and so may replacing the sensor's battery with a fresh one. In the worst case, you may need a different sensor brand.

3. The sensor reacts to pressure changes, but fails to detect wheel rotation (if it has rotation detection). Swapping it with a sensor that reports regularly helps tell this apart from #2: if it still doesn't send updates from where the other one does, it's likely faulty and should be replaced. You can use "Manage sensors" in the vehicle settings to quickly move them between the wheels.

If the sensor reports battery voltage, you can set when to report it as low. Within 0.1 V of the setting, it\'s shown in orange. After 10 minutes of consistently low readings it will raise an alert. The app will use a slightly reduced value when temperatures are low, to account for the voltage drop.

Lowers the screen\'s brightness on the main screen once nothing new was alerted or warned about for a while. A red or critical alert going on keeps it bright, a new alert or warning brings it back up. When dimmed, a first touch only brightens the screen, lift your finger and touch again to use the app.

Most TPMS sensors send updates at regular time intervals while riding. However, in some cases the updates can get lost, because of signal obstruction, low sensor battery or other issues. Knowing when exactly the last update arrived from each sensor can help you diagnose these issues.

When a sensor reports pressure outside of the range set here, it will raise an alert and blink the affected tyre indicator in red. If it\'s more than 20% above the maximum, or more than 25% below the minimum, it will be a critical alert. Getting within 3% of the minimum or maximum will raise a warning.

When no Bluetooth connections or beacons are configured to activate persistent scanning, it will run background scanning all or nearly all the time, which increases battery drain.\n\nConsider figuring out which Bluetooth device or beacon can be used for that purpose in your vehicle, or use manual (non-persistent) mode if you want to avoid that.
